source_sentences: Any term of an employment or independent-contractor agreement that prohibits or restricts a worker, after the work relationship ends, from working for another person or carrying on a business, or that imposes a penalty for doing so, is void.
The Act binds employers of workers who primarily work in Teravel, whatever law the contract chooses.
This applies to agreements made before, on or after the effective date, and pending cases are decided under the Act.
A worker may sue an employer that tries to enforce a void term, or puts one in a contract after the effective date.
There is no new appropriation; the Bureau works from its existing budget.
Every employer that has a non-compete with a current worker, or with a former worker who left after 1 January 2024, must give written notice by 1 March 2026 that the term is void.

context: A 2024 survey by the state labor department found that about 17% had signed a non-compete clause.
Until now Teravel courts enforced "reasonable" non-competes (up to two years, within the employer's trading area) under common law.

readings: U1-a: yes, any paid notice period in which the worker remains employed is preserved
U1-b: no, a notice period long enough to keep the worker out of the field is a restraint "in effect", and is void
unclear.text: Does the exemption for "a notice period during which the worker remains employed" cover a notice period of six to twelve months, paid in full, with no duties, during which the worker may not work for anyone else?

readings: U2-a: yes, it penalizes leaving, and leaving is how one comes to work for another
U2-b: no, it applies to every departure, whatever the worker does next, and only recovers a cost
unclear.text: Is a term that requires a worker who leaves within 24 months to repay employer-paid training a "penalty" for working for another person?
